title: Environmental Sensor Networks
keywords_for_the_page_and_card: Instrumentation · Open hardware · Telemetry · Long-term monitoring
intro: A measurement is only useful if it survives the winter. We build open-hardware sensors that keep reporting when nobody is there to fix them.
add_focus_list: Sub-zero power budgets and anti-fouling design
Public data APIs with versioned calibration records
add_paragraph:
Commercial environmental sensors are expensive, closed and rarely designed for a Norwegian winter. Our group builds its own: modular boards, open firmware and calibration routines that can be repeated in any partner lab.

The network now spans nine sites, from rooftop aerosol monitors in Oslo to coastal observatories in the Oslofjord and an alpine station above the tree line. Every node publishes raw counts alongside calibrated values, so a downstream user can decide for themselves how much to trust the number.
